items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: Melissa Hayden from the classical dance era

ctx.x: And three and all kinds of changes while people were trying to play -- well, you went through another -- the other side of the coin, too, from spontaneous composition, in that period when you were with Teo Macero T.O. Vessero and the real Workshop, the Jazz Workshop, was named after, I guess. I remember, I think you were quoted by somebody as saying, "Write it out, write it out." Mingus means And so you just insisted that everybody in that group write everything that they were feeling out and not leave anything…

Yeah. That's when I had that superb energy to want to do something like that. Because it wasn't just talk to say -- to do a operatic ballet, with tap dances from the Baby Laurence (inaudible) era. And -- well, in those times, Melissa Hayden from the classical dance era, Katherine Dunham from the modern
dance era. It wasn't just for fun I was saying that, just to talk. I really wanted to do it, but I couldn't ever get anybody with enough foresight to WANT TO get together and do it.
